available_outcomes.name: Head injury-related death within 24 h of injury
available_outcomes.source_quote: Because early head injury-related deaths are more likely to result from intracranial haemorrhage than are late head injury-related deaths, we examined the effect of tranexamic acid on head injury-related death within 24 h of injury. The RR of head injury-related death was 0·81 (95% CI 0·69–0·95) within 24 h.

available_outcomes.name: Head injury-related death within 24 h of injury (excluding GCS 3 or bilateral unreactive pupils)
available_outcomes.source_quote: When patients with a GCS score of 3 and those with bilateral unreactive pupils at baseline were excluded, the RR was 0·72 (0·56–0·92) within 24 h.

available_outcomes.name: Non-head injury-related deaths
available_outcomes.source_quote: The RR for non-head injury-related deaths was 1·31 (95% CI 0·93–1·85)

available_outcomes.name: All-cause mortality
available_outcomes.source_quote: and 0·96 (0·89–1·04) for all-cause mortality.

quotes.randomization: An independent statistician from Sealed Envelope (London, UK) prepared the randomisation codes... We randomly allocated eligible patients to receive tranexamic acid or matching placebo... by selecting a numbered treatment pack...
quotes.deviations: Patients, caregivers, and those assessing outcomes were masked to allocation... Ampoules and packaging were identical in appearance.
quotes.missingData: We enrolled 9202 (72·2%) patients within 3 h of injury... We did not obtain primary outcome data for 75 (0·8%) patients.
quotes.measurement: The primary outcome was head injury-related death... Cause of death was assessed by the responsible clinician... blind to the trial treatment.
quotes.reporting: We published a statistical analysis plan before unblinding... All analyses were on an intention-to-treat basis.
